# Decision history — legeos

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## legeos.decision.base-ubuntu-2604-kernel-70

### Revision 1 — D1/ADR-0007 — Base is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'resolute' with Ubuntu's linux-generic 7.0; mainline 7.2 only as a transaction candidate

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.base-ubuntu-2604-kernel-70/1` · scope `path "distro/**"` · topic `base-and-kernel`

The base is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ('resolute') declared once in distro/base.toml; the kernel is Ubuntu's linux-generic (7.0 GA, HWE later), version-locked with Canonical-signed prebuilt NVIDIA LRM modules (linux-modules-nvidia-<branch>-generic) and firmware by the legeos-kernel / legeos-nvidia-{open,proprietary} metapackages. Mainline 7.2 is never hand-installed; it is a candidate for lege-hostd's kernel/NVIDIA transaction path.

**Context.** Ubuntu 26.04 = resolute, kernel 7.0 (renumbered 6.20). The planning docs advise against placing upstream 7.2 on a hybrid Intel/NVIDIA laptop that already saw driver conflicts; reproducible driver validation and rollback matter more than kernel recency.

**Consequences.** One declarative base; NVIDIA via Ubuntu LRM (no DKMS, no .run installer); newer kernels only through the transactional path with the hardware matrix green.

## legeos.decision.boot-deploy-secure-boot

### Revision 1 — D5/ADR-0004 — Kernel/NVIDIA transactions on btrfs deployments with systemd boot assessment and a system-scope health probe; Secure-Boot posture open until Stage 3

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.boot-deploy-secure-boot/1` · scope `path "distro/deploy/**"`, `path "distro/image/**"`, `path "services/lege-boot-health/**"`, `path "services/lege-hostd/src/deploy.rs"` · topic `boot-deployments`

Root is btrfs subvolumes from the first mkosi repart layout; a deployment is a read-only snapshot plus a hostd-owned ESP directory (/EFI/legeos/<id>/) holding kernel, initrd and entry, so kernel + NVIDIA modules + userspace roll back together and Ubuntu's initramfs hooks cannot rewrite the previous entry. Kernels stay Ubuntu-signed Type #1 entries (no self-built UKI). A candidate boots with a boot-assessment counter; lege-boot-health (SYSTEM scope, before boot-complete.target, TimeoutStartSec + FailureAction=reboot-force) gates systemd-bless-boot. A BootManager trait has two backends: systemd-boot (bless-boot) and grub (GRUB_DEFAULT=saved + grub-reboot + hostd counter). Dev/VM images use systemd-boot with Secure Boot off. OPEN before Stage 3 on real hardware: (a) LegeOS-signed systemd-boot + MOK enrolment at install, (b) Canonical-signed GRUB + hostd counter, (c) SB off dev-only; and snapshot vs A/B for Stage 4.

**Context.** Ubuntu 26.04 ships systemd-boot but no Canonical-signed variant, so shim will not chain to it under Secure Boot without a MOK; a boot entry alone does not roll back NVIDIA userspace on a shared root.

**Consequences.** The docs' 8-step watchdog sequence reuses systemd primitives; the deployment layout is fixed early (cheap now, expensive later); the Secure-Boot choice is explicit, not accidental.

## legeos.decision.debian-packaging

### Revision 1 — D9/ADR-0009 — Packaging: cargo-deb per binary now; one vendored source package (root debian/) for the archive; keyring + pins as legeos-archive-keyring

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.debian-packaging/1` · scope `path "debian/**"`, `path "distro/apt/**"`, `path "distro/metapackages/**"`, `path "packaging/**"` · topic `debian-packaging`

Stage 1: every binary crate carries [package.metadata.deb]; `cargo deb -p <crate>` feeds a local aptly repo (never /usr/local). Stage 2: one source package `legeos` with debian/ at the repo root, vendor/ shipped in the orig tarball, dh_auto_build overridden with `cargo build --release --frozen --offline --workspace`; metapackages in legeos-meta; legeos-archive-keyring ships the archive key, deb822 legeos.sources and preferences.d pins rejecting third-party driver repositories. dh-cargo is not used.

**Context.** dh-cargo expects Debian-packaged crates — impractical for zbus 5 / tokio 1.5x / smithay; vendoring is what COSMIC's own packaging does.

**Consequences.** Packages from day one; the archive path is ready when the repository exists.

## legeos.decision.flatpak-and-crash-handling

### Revision 1 — D11/ADR-0011 — Flatpak for sandboxed apps (no snapd in the seeds); telemetry-free crash handling via systemd-coredump ingested into history

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.flatpak-and-crash-handling/1` · scope `path "distro/policy/coredump/**"`, `path "distro/seeds/**"` · topic `app-distribution-and-crashes`

Sandboxed applications come as Flatpak (the alias model carries Flatpak IDs); snapd is excluded from the seeds and legeos-desktop conflicts with it. Crash handling: systemd-coredump on, apport/whoopsie out; lege-sessiond ingests coredump journal entries (PID -> cgroup -> instance) into the event history so a crash is one explainable, restorable event.

**Context.** Ubuntu forces the snap decision (Firefox/Thunderbird are snaps); the docs forbid 'a complete alternative application store' — Flatpak/Flathub is not that; the docs want notifications and system decisions as searchable history.

**Consequences.** One sandbox format in the identity model; crashes are attributed to instances without any upload.

## legeos.decision.forks-by-manifest

### Revision 1 — D6/ADR-0005 — Upstream forks (cosmic-comp, cosmic-files, cosmic portal, cosmic-greeter, cosmic-applets) are pinned by distro/forks/manifest.toml, not git submodules

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.forks-by-manifest/1` · scope `path "apps/lege-files/**"`, `path "compositor/**"`, `path "distro/forks/**"` · topic `upstream-forks`

Each fork lives in its own repository with an 'upstream' tracking branch and a 'legeos' patch branch; distro/forks/manifest.toml pins URL/branch/commit; `just forks-fetch` clones into the gitignored forks/ directory. compositor/lege-comp-integration is a path crate the compositor fork depends on; the files fork depends on lege-client. Patches are limited to the items enumerated in compositor/FORK.md and apps/lege-files/FORK.md.

**Context.** The user's four separately maintained COSMIC submodules already caused rebase and detached-HEAD problems; Stage 2 wants proper downstream repos with automated rebase checks.

**Consequences.** No submodule state in this repository; reproducible builds from the manifest; monthly rebase cadence.

## legeos.decision.mkosi-images

### Revision 1 — D7/ADR-0006 — mkosi builds the dev/CI/VM disk image (ESP + btrfs subvolumes); the installer ISO is a later stage

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.mkosi-images/1` · scope `path "distro/image/**"`, `path "distro/iso/**"`, `path "distro/seeds/**"` · topic `image-build`

distro/image/mkosi.conf: Distribution=ubuntu Release=resolute Repositories=main,universe,restricted Format=disk Bootable=yes Bootloader=systemd-boot UnifiedKernelImages=no ToolsTree=default, mkosi.repart/ with ESP + btrfs subvolumes, packages composed from distro/seeds/*.seed by compose.sh. mkosi has no ISO output; the installer ISO comes later via ubuntu-image classic or live-build from the same seeds.

**Context.** Native Ubuntu support, UKI/signed systemd-boot options and systemd-repart give a straight path to snapshot/A-B deployments; the host currently lacks mkosi (apt install mkosi on 26.04).

**Consequences.** One declarative image definition, `mkosi vm` for tests; image build itself is out of scope for M0.

## legeos.decision.one-privileged-host-daemon

### Revision 1 — D4/ADR-0003 — One privileged host daemon (lege-hostd): updates, deployments, driver authority, storage reserve, hardware profile; timezone policy stays in sessiond

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.one-privileged-host-daemon/1` · scope `path "distro/policy/dbus/**"`, `path "distro/policy/polkit/**"`, `path "services/lege-hostd/**"` · topic `privileged-host-daemon`

lege-hostd (system bus org.legeos.Host, one polkit policy org.legeos.host.*, AppArmor profile) hosts Updates, Deployments (BootManager trait), Drivers/GPU mode, Storage reserve and Hardware profile. It keeps an on-disk transaction journal and runs apt as a child transient unit. Timezone/location policy is NOT in hostd: it is network-facing and lives in lege-sessiond, setting the zone via polkit-gated org.freedesktop.timedate1.

**Context.** The docs' updated, 'one driver authority', storage reserve and locationd are all root policy over apt/systemd; each as its own root daemon multiplies privileged surfaces; untrusted geolocation JSON must not be parsed as root.

**Consequences.** Fewer privileged surfaces; one place for lege update, doctor support-violation checks and the hardware profile.

## legeos.decision.one-session-policy-daemon

### Revision 1 — D2/ADR-0001 — One user session policy daemon (lege-sessiond) hosting appd, associationd, providers, history, notifications, settings, projects, power, location as library crates

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.one-session-policy-daemon/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-appd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-associationd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-session-core/**"`, `path "crates/lege-state/**"`, `path "services/lege-sessiond/**"` · topic `session-policy-daemon`

lege-sessiond is the single user policy daemon (bus name org.legeos.Session). Application identity + launching (appd), the association broker (associationd), provider/autostart arbitration, history, notifications (org.freedesktop.Notifications when selected), typed settings, project sessions, power and timezone/location policy are separate library crates wired by a thin daemon over one SQLite state store (lege-state). Interfaces are domain-scoped and versioned (org.legeos.AppIdentity1, org.legeos.Associations1, ...) at separate object paths so a later split only relocates a bus name. Type=notify, Restart=on-failure, WatchdogSec; instances persisted and re-derived from systemd unit patterns after restart; history writes are non-fatal.

**Context.** The planning docs propose several services and note associationd 'probably as part of appd'; the user's Lubuntu install suffers from many daemons/applets with private state and no shared identity key; cross-daemon D-Bus adds the launch-registration and governor-blocking races the docs flag.

**Consequences.** One crash/restart unit and one place to explain decisions; cross-domain updates are transactions. filed and resourced remain separate processes. Crate boundaries keep the split reversible.

## legeos.decision.resourced-separate-process

### Revision 1 — D3/ADR-0002 — The resource governor (lege-resourced) is a separate, tiny, protected process that needs no D-Bus for emergency actions

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.resourced-separate-process/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-types/src/unit.rs"`, `path "services/lege-resourced/**"` · topic `resource-governor-process`

lege-resourced runs as its own user process (org.legeos.Resources) with mlockall, MemoryLow, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, high CPU/IO weight and no SQLite. Launch units are self-describing (app-legeos-<AppId>@<InstanceId>.service) so cgroup->instance identity is derived from /sys/fs/cgroup alone; foreground/visibility arrive as compositor signals; sessiond only enriches. Policy is a pure engine separated from cgroup writes and runs observe-only until recorded traces show sensible choices; then cache trim, throttling (memory.high + reclaim), checkpoint requests and whole-cgroup termination are enabled in stages.

**Context.** The governor must keep ticking under exactly the conditions that stall a daemon doing SQLite/fsync/D-Bus/desktop-file imports (full disk in the storage-reserve case, a panic in an unrelated domain).

**Consequences.** Two user daemons for policy instead of one; the governor is testable in isolation and survives sessiond restarts; lege doctor verifies its protection values.

## legeos.decision.session-greeter-lock

### Revision 1 — D10/ADR-0010 — systemd-managed session (legeos-session.target), sessiond-arbitrated autostart, greetd + cosmic-greeter, compositor-owned lock screen

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.session-greeter-lock/1` · scope `path "session/**"` · topic `session-assembly`

The session is legeos-session.target plus user units with explicit protection values, started by the lege-session entry from wayland-sessions/legeos.desktop; xdg-desktop-autostart.target is masked and lege-sessiond launches approved autostart entries with identity and cgroups (one provider per exclusive role). Greeter: greetd + the cosmic-greeter fork (reuses the compositor). Lock screen: compositor-core ext-session-lock-v1.

**Context.** A full distribution needs a display manager and a session manager; reusing the compositor for the greeter avoids a second toolkit stack; the docs demand permissioned autostart and one provider per role.

**Consequences.** One session stack; lege doctor checks the units and their protection values.

## legeos.decision.toolchain-licence-namespace

### Revision 1 — D8/ADR-0008 — Rust 2024 edition, dev toolchain 1.97.1, MSRV 1.93 (Ubuntu 26.04 rustc), MPL-2.0 for own code, org.legeos namespace

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.toolchain-licence-namespace/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "LICENSE"`, `path "crates/lege-types/src/dbus.rs"`, `path "deny.toml"`, `path "rust-toolchain.toml"` · topic `toolchain-licence-namespace`

Edition 2024, resolver 3; rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 for development; workspace rust-version = "1.93" (Ubuntu 26.04's rustc) with an MSRV CI job. Own code is MPL-2.0 (repository-wide LICENSE); forks keep upstream GPL-3.0; deny.toml holds the licence allow-list; DEP-5 debian/copyright is regenerated by cargo xtask copyright. Reverse-DNS namespace org.legeos for D-Bus names, app IDs and first-party apps (org.legeos.Session/.Resources/.Files/.Host; org.legeos.Files, org.legeos.Viewer); polkit org.legeos.host.*; env LEGEOS_APP_ID / LEGEOS_INSTANCE_ID.

**Context.** The planning workspace used edition 2024 + MPL-2.0 and org.example placeholders; the archive build must work with the distribution's own rustc.

**Consequences.** One namespace everywhere; archive-buildable without a newer toolchain.
